verdicts.reason: Both have the same problems: the SUNSET SALE eyebrow drops below the body copy, so the reading order is broken. The legal line sits on the brown ellipse. The CTA rides over the decorative circle and runs nearly into the right edge. A's can is small and sits loose at the far left. B's larger can balances the left side better, but B's legal text wraps onto two lines that sit right on the ellipse.

A's SOLSTICE wordmark is broken ('SOLST CE') where the sun icon cuts into it. A's can is cramped against the right edge, and its CTA sits on the decorative circle. B keeps the wordmark intact and has a better-balanced can. B still has SUNSET SALE below the subhead, legal text in two lines on the ellipse, and the CTA on the circle near the edge.

A has the usual flaws: SUNSET SALE sits under the subhead, legal text sits on the ellipse, the can is small, and the CTA rides the circle. Its hierarchy is still coherent. B blows the headline up so far that 'OFF' nearly touches the CTA. B's logo shrinks to an illegible speck at the bottom, its legal text moves to the top as the first thing read, and SUNSET SALE becomes tiny text on the ellipse.

A has an oversized headline. Its logo is reduced to an unreadable speck at the bottom, the fine print sits at the top, the CTA is jammed against the left edge on the circle, and SUNSET SALE is tiny. B keeps a sensible headline/subhead/CTA hierarchy, but its wordmark is broken ('SOLST CE'), SUNSET SALE sits below the subhead on the ellipse, and the can hugs the right edge.
